summary.plain: The final results of the MEG experiment, from its full 2009-2013 dataset: no significant excess of events over the expected background in the search for a very rare muon decay into a positron and a photon. The paper calls the resulting upper limit the most stringent limit on the existence of this decay to date.
summary.technical: Final results on the full 2009-2013 dataset (7.5×10¹⁴ stopped muons on target): no significant excess over the expected background; BR(μ⁺→e⁺γ) < 4.2×10⁻¹³ at 90% C.L., which the paper says is the most stringent limit on the existence of this decay to date.

title: Search for the Lepton Flavour Violating Decay mu+ -> e+ gamma with the Full Dataset of the MEG Experiment
why_it_matters: The paper's introduction says the Standard Model allows charged lepton flavour violating processes such as this only with extremely small branching ratios, even accounting for measured neutrino masses and mixing angles, so such decays are free from Standard Model physics backgrounds associated with processes involving hadronic states, and a positive signal would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model.
